title: Novel antioxidant peptides from jellyfish (Nemopilema nomurai) hydrolysate: identification, activity, and potential mechanisms.
authors: Shen, Wen; Wang, Xueqin; Liu, Xiaoxiao; Li, Rongfeng; Liu, Song; Xing, Ronge; Yu, Huahua
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦水母源抗氧化肽的鉴定与活性，分子对接仅涉及肽-Keap1蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: To explore the antioxidant function and application potential of bioactive peptides derived from jellyfish, this study focused on the identification, activity, and potential mechanisms of novel antioxidant peptides from JP-FC, a peptide fraction prepared via enzymatic hydrolysis of jellyfish Nemopilema nomurai. JP-FC exhibited potent antioxidant capacity, with EC(50) of 1.03, 2.05, and 4.94 mg/mL against hydroxyl radicals (.OH), superoxide anion radicals (O(2)(-).), and 1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl radicals (DPPH.), respectively. LC-MS/MS combined with bioinformatic analysis identified three key peptides, FNPPPP, PPPMQPPP, and WDAPLLG, which exhibited EC(50) values of 0.86, 1.25, and 1.69 mg/mL, respectively, in hydroxyl radical scavenging assays. In a H(2)O(2)-induced oxidative stress model in immortalized human keratinocytes (HaCaT cells), FNPPPP, and PPPMQPPP significantly decreased intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels while enhancing superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, demonstrating strong antioxidant and cytoprotective effects. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions between these peptides and Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1), implying a possible association with nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)-related antioxidant regulation that warrants further experimental validation. The RT-qPCR analysis showed that peptide treatment modulated the transcriptional expression of Keap1 and downstream antioxidant-response genes (HO-1 and NQO1) under oxidative stress conditions. Overall, the novel antioxidant peptides in JP-FC indicate that JP-FC is a promising natural antioxidant source, providing a scientific foundation for the development of jellyfish-derived peptides in functional food, cosmetic and pharmaceuticals. Moreover, this study supports the high-value utilization of jellyfish biomass by highlighting its dual dietary and health-promoting potential as a traditional food resource with nutraceutical relevance. Further work is required to enhance peptide stability and verify antioxidant mechanisms under physiologically relevant conditions.
abstract_zh: 为探究水母源生物活性肽的抗氧化功能及应用潜力，本研究聚焦于通过酶解水母Nemopilema nomurai制备的肽组分JP-FC中新型抗氧化肽的鉴定、活性及潜在机制。JP-FC表现出强效抗氧化能力，对羟基自由基(.OH)、超氧阴离子自由基(O(2)(-).)和1,1-二苯基-2-苦肼基自由基(DPPH.)的EC(50)值分别为1.03、2.05和4.94 mg/mL。结合LC-MS/MS与生物信息学分析，鉴定出三种关键肽FNPPPP、PPPMQPPP和WDAPLLG，其在羟基自由基清除实验中分别表现出0.86、1.25和1.69 mg/mL的EC(50)值。在永生化人角质形成细胞（HaCaT细胞）的H(2)O(2)诱导氧化应激模型中，FNPPPP和PPPMQPPP显著降低细胞内活性氧（ROS）和丙二醛（MDA）水平，同时增强超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）活性，展现出强效抗氧化和细胞保护作用。分子对接提示这些肽与Kelch样ECH相关蛋白1（Keap1）之间存在潜在相互作用，暗示其可能与核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）相关的抗氧化调控有关，有待进一步实验验证。RT-qPCR分析显示，在氧化应激条件下，肽处理调节了Keap1及下游抗氧化响应基因（HO-1和NQO1）的转录表达。总体而言，JP-FC中的新型抗氧化肽表明JP-FC是一种有前景的天然抗氧化源，为水母源肽在功能性食品、化妆品和药品中的开发提供了科学基础。此外，本研究通过强调水母作为传统食物资源兼具膳食和健康促进双重潜力，支持了水母生物质的高值化利用。未来需进一步工作以提高肽稳定性，并在生理相关条件下验证抗氧化机制。
